interval_model.copy_rule: margins read 'at least this wide', never plus-or-minus

variance_model_phase1.note: the Phase 1 per-metro power law is retired; its 44% p90 failure and diagnostics remain in results/phase1/variance_validation.json

tier_policy.suppress: min(n_alloc, kish) < 100, or empty pool — the gate is n alone (ADR 0002; the rival condition left with the rival apparatus, ADR 0004)
tier_policy.shown_unranked: permanently empty: the CV tiers are removed (measured max true CV 11.8%, p99 9.8% in the served region of the 480-shape battery — the rules could not fire)
tier_policy.ranked: everything else in the ranked set; margins are computed and returned but no longer rendered (ADR 0004) — suppression is the visible expression of uncertainty
tier_policy.balance_gate: dating pool balance gates separately: both age-by-sex counts must clear the same 100-effective-respondent bar
tier_policy.match_gate: chances of matching gates on the UNWEIGHTED n of the same masked pool (ADR 0009): the kernel can neither rescue nor condemn a cell

kernel.form: three forms (ADR 0018). Race on (the seeker's race given): w = exp(theta_age f_age(gap; sex_s, cohort) + theta_edu f_edu + theta_race f_race + g(race x edu) + log_norm), C1 as m3.5.0 serves it. Race off: w = exp(theta_age rf_f_age(gap; sex_s, cohort) + theta_edu rf_f_edu + rf_log_norm), no race term, no interaction. Same-sex: w = exp(ss_f_age(gap; sex_s) + ss_f_edu + ss_log_norm), no race term, no interaction, no dial
kernel.gauge: each main effect: availability-weighted mean multiplier 1 on its own margin under random pairing (age per sex x cohort); the interaction is centred by its zero-mean prior; log_norm makes the full kernel average exactly 1 over the national single adult population of the sought sex per seeker type

fitting_sample_spec.weight: (CASE WHEN married THEN power(0.5, (svy_year - union_year) / 5.0) ELSE 1.0 END)

normalization.extensive: winsorize -> log10 -> min-max across the ranked set for this query
normalization.intensive: percentile rank across the ranked set for this query

strings.home_title: Which city has the best dating scene for you?
strings.home_subtitle: See how many singles in each US metro match what you're looking for, and how each city ranks for you. Based on Census data.
strings.slider_info: Leaning towards size favors larger cities with the most possible matches. Leaning towards compatibility favors cities with people who match your search more closely on age, education, and background, based on historical Census couples data.
strings.match_how: The compatibility figure is built from real couples in the Census Bureau's household survey, using each partner's age and education, and their race or ethnicity only if you include yours. Across the whole country we measure how often each age gap and each education pairing actually occurs, compared with how often it would occur if single people paired at random; if you include your race or ethnicity, the racial and ethnic pairings are measured the same way. That pattern, adjusted a little for each city's own couples, is then applied to the single people who match your search in each city, so the figure says how closely they resemble the people who typically pair with someone of your sex, age and education, and background if you include it. It is an aggregate pattern from recent unions, not a prediction about any one person, and 100 is the US average for your search.
strings.match_same_sex_note: For a same-sex search the age gaps and the education pairings come from same-sex couples in the same survey; the racial and ethnic pairings are not used, even if you include your race or ethnicity.
strings.match_same_sex_note_all_fallback: For a same-sex search the age gaps, the education pairings and the racial and ethnic pairings all come from opposite-sex couples, because same-sex couples in the survey are too few to measure them on their own.
strings.self_race_same_sex_tip: This information is not used to calculate compatibility for same-sex couples because not enough data is available to make a reliable estimate.
strings.self_race_same_sex_tip_label: Why race or ethnicity isn't used here
strings.credits_photos_more: Photographs on the home, city and stat pages ({n})
strings.crime_caution: The FBI cautions against using this number to compare cities. Data can be affected by how much crime is reported and whether local agencies send data to the FBI at all.
strings.crime_coverage_line: Police agencies covering {coverage} of the people here reported a full year of {year} data. The rates count only what those agencies cover.
strings.crime_blank: Not enough of {city}'s police agencies reported a full year of data for a figure we'd stand behind, so none is shown.
strings.crime_compare_note: Read each city's crime figures on their own. Different shares of each city's police agencies report, so the two columns aren't comparable — the FBI itself cautions against comparisons like that.
strings.crime_compare_banner: The FBI cautions against using these numbers to compare cities. Data can be affected by how much crime is reported and whether local agencies send data to the FBI at all.
strings.crime_card_blank: Not enough police reporting here for a figure worth showing.
strings.stat_page_missing: {n} of the ranked cities don't have this figure and are left off this list rather than shown as zero.
strings.age_range_error: Ages run 18 to 70 here — that's the survey's own range.
strings.measure_crime_note: Crime reported per 100,000 people a year (not used to calculate city rankings)
strings.stat_strip_label: How the figures spread across every ranked city
strings.compare_default_note: This comparison uses the site's starting search: {search}. Set your own on the home page and it follows you here.
strings.compare_page_subtitle: View two cities side by side. Learn how each ranks in your search, and see every city's stats with the differences between them.
strings.compare_diff_legend: Green means the difference favors {a} for your search; red means it favors {b}. Grey means we don't judge it: population is just a fact, and a measure you set to "Not much" still counts toward the score — it just matters least to you.
strings.results_count: {n} metro areas ranked for your search, each scored out of 100
strings.find_in_results: Find a city in your results
strings.balance_short_caption: All singles in your age range, before other filters
strings.moved_caption: Compared with the middle of the cities ranked for this search
strings.explainer_lifestyle: Lifestyle: Four things you weight: cost of living, social life, student life and weather.
strings.same_sex_pool_note: On a same-sex search, matches count every single {sought_one} in these ages. The Census doesn't ask who people date, so only some of them are looking for {sought}.
strings.balance_caption_same_sex: Balance compares all single men with all single women in the ages you picked. On a same-sex search it describes the city, not your matches.
strings.sharpen_info: Optional. These change the compatibility figure only. They stay on this device: the site sends the figures for every combination, and your browser shows yours.
strings.compare_edge_note: Edge names the city that does better on each measure for your search, and by how much. A dash means we don't judge that measure.
strings.city_below_floor: {city} has fewer than 250,000 people, so it isn't ranked; the site ranks metro areas of 250,000 or more. Its profile is below.
strings.not_found_body: There is no page at this address.

pool_size.definition: The number of people in each city who match your whole search, estimated from the Census Bureau's household survey.

pool_balance.definition: Number of single men per 100 single women in your selected age range (or the opposite, if you're looking for women)

match_propensity.definition: How closely the people who match your search resemble the people who actually pair with someone like you, on age, education, and background, where 100 is the US average

provenance.table: pool_cube x kernel (person+household couple links, RELSHIPP 20<->21/22)

partners_per_rival.definition: Retired in m2.0.0. For every 10 people looking for the same kind of match, how many people fit your filters.
partners_per_rival.retired_reason: Read as the city's sex ratio when it was pool-over-competition after every filter; replaced by pool_balance, the plain sex ratio (ADR 0004, m2.0.0).

rent_1br.definition: The typical monthly rent for a one-bedroom home across the city, utilities included

rpp_goods.definition: Price level for goods, where the US average is 100 (BEA).

rpp_services_other.definition: Price level for services other than housing, where the US average is 100 (BEA).

everyday_prices.definition: The price of goods and services, where the US average is 100.

venues_per_100k.unit: bars, cafés and venues per 100,000 adults
venues_per_100k.definition: Restaurants, coffee shops, bars, gyms, museums and movie theaters per 100,000 adults

resident_walkability_index.stat_page_note: The EPA's index scores each neighborhood on how connected its streets are, how close it is to public transit, and how mixed its homes, shops and workplaces are. A city's figure averages those scores over where its residents live.
resident_walkability_index.definition: A walkability index of where the city's residents live, from 1 to 20.

poi_venue_density.definition: Deferred: a POI-based venue count awaiting the coverage-bias regression against Census business data. Not computed and not scored.

pleasant_days.unit: days that are mild and dry enough to be outside
pleasant_days.definition: Days a year that average between 55 and 75°F, stay below 85°F and above 45°F, and have no more than a light shower and no snow

students_per_1k_adults.definition: Students enrolled at the city's colleges per 1,000 adults, not counting online-only enrollment

who_lives_here.definition: Everyone living in the metro area, and how many are adults aged 18 to 70.

political_lean.definition: How the metro area voted in the 2024 presidential election. It describes everyone who voted there, not the people who match your search.

provenance.dataset: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, County Presidential Election Returns 2000-2024 (V20)

cross_group_pairing_rate.definition: Retired in m2.0.0. Among partnered people of a group, the share whose spouse or partner is outside that group.
cross_group_pairing_rate.retired_reason: Race filters carry no claim about who partners with whom (ADR 0004); retired from serving in m2.0.0. pairing_cells.parquet and the couples linkage remain for Phase 3.

violent_crime_rate.definition: Murder, rape, robbery and aggravated assault reported to police, per 100,000 people in the areas whose agencies reported a full year (FBI Crime Data Explorer).

property_crime_rate.definition: Burglary, larceny-theft and motor vehicle theft reported to police, per 100,000 people in the areas whose agencies reported a full year (FBI Crime Data Explorer).

crime_coverage.unit: of people here live in areas whose police reported a full year
crime_coverage.definition: The share of the metro's population living in areas whose police agencies reported a full year of data — the reason crime figures aren't comparable between cities.
